files.note: Defines the algebra-valued inner structure and its norm compatibility; add the existing CompleteSpace condition for Hilbert modules.

formalizations.evidence:
Mathlib commit 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. CStarModule:73 in Module/Defs.lean supplies the positive definite algebra-valued inner product and compatibility with the induced norm. It does not include completeness: the catalogue object is explicitly the conjunction CStarModule Aᵐᵒᵖ E and CompleteSpace E. CompleteSpace is the checked existing Cauchy-completeness predicate, not an inferred property of every CStarModule. Source statements and relevant proof bodies inspected; no fresh Lean build or transitive axiom audit. Explicit RIGHT-MODULE convention: instantiate the checked class at coefficient algebra Aᵐᵒᵖ. For the catalogue right A-action y*a, use (MulOpposite.op a) • y := y*a, and take its opposite-valued inner product to be MulOpposite.op of the catalogue inner product B(x,y). The class law inner_op_smul_right:80 reads innerOpp x ((op a)•y)=(op a)*innerOpp x y, hence, because multiplication in the opposite algebra reverses order, exactly B(x,y*a)=B(x,y)*a. Star symmetry and complex linearity in y are preserved: MulOpposite.op_star:600 (Algebra/Star/Basic), opposite module structure (Algebra/Module/Opposite.instModule:46), and norm_op:561 (Analysis/Normed/Group/Constructions) identify star, scalar multiplication and the induced norm without conjugating the complex action. Opposite order is the transported order, and Algebra/Order/Star/Basic:398 proves StarOrderedRing on Aᵐᵒᵖ; Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Basic:225 proves CStarRing on the opposite. Thus positivity and separation, and CompleteSpace where required, are unchanged. A raw CStarModule A E would express left multiplication in its second-slot scalar law; the opposite-algebra instantiation is the exact right-A interpretation. These source suppliers were checked in the fixed Mathlib snapshot; Module/Defs and native extensionality are the already checked exact dependency/native files. No separately named right-Hilbert alias or new mathematical theorem is required.
